question: ________ is known as “Saffron town" of Kashmir.
solution:
The correct answer is **Pampore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pampore** is a town in the Pulwama district of Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The town is famously known as the **"Saffron town"** due to its extensive saffron cultivation.
 
• **Saffron** from Pampore is considered one of the best in the world due to its high quality and distinct flavor.
 
• The cultivation of saffron in Pampore dates back to ancient times and is an integral part of the region's heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Saffron Cultivation**
 The process of growing saffron involves planting corms of the saffron crocus in well-drained soil, usually in the summer, and harvesting the delicate stigmas in autumn.
 
 

 **Economic Importance**
 Saffron is a highly valuable spice, often referred to as "red gold." It plays a significant role in the local economy of Pampore.
 
 

 **Historical Significance**
 Pampore's association with saffron cultivation dates back to ancient times. Historical records suggest it was introduced by Persian settlers.
 
 

 **Cultural Impact**
 Saffron is deeply embedded in the cultural fabric of Kashmir. It is used in traditional cuisine, ceremonies, and as a medicinal herb.
